Every API detail. No endpoint path, query parameter, auth requirement, rate limit or response schema for api.bmrb.io appears in either attached file. The BMRB-API docs must be read live first - the map's own instruction is "Confirm the official API schemas rather than guessing routes."

Whether structure-based lookup exists at all: can a record be found by InChI/InChIKey/SMILES, or only by BMRB metabolomics accession, compound name or an external ID? Without this, find_structure cannot be implemented.

How exact-molecule identity is represented per record (salt form, protonation state, tautomer, isotopic labelling, stereochemistry), since the map requires "exact molecule / different protonation, salt, tautomer, isotope or stereoisomer" to be stored as distinct states.

Which field distinguishes experimental from theoretical entries, and whether that field is exposed through the API rather than only rendered in the portal. The map warns the portal mixes both and that the distinction must be preserved.
Whether peaks carry atom-level assignments mapped to a specific structure's atom numbering, or are unassigned/partially assigned peak lists. The map only says to "verify assignments ... per record".

Whether solvent, temperature, pH, chemical-shift reference compound and referencing method, nucleus and spectrometer frequency exist as structured per-record fields - and, where absent, whether they are genuinely absent upstream or dropped by an export/parser (the map requires that audit explicitly).

Exact reuse terms: which BMRB archive/data terms govern the metabolomics subset, whether CC0 or any license is actually asserted, and whether redistribution and the intended downstream use are permitted. The registry has automated_ingestion_approved: false and the policy page is documented as not specifying a standard reuse license.
Whether raw/time-domain data is retrievable over HTTPS from bmrb.io or only via ftp.bmrb.io, plus per-file sizes and counts, so a bounded byte/file cap can be set before any download.

Registry key mismatch: this source is stored in NMRx_Chemical_Source_Registry.json as id "bmrb" (entry number 5), not "bmrb_metabolomics". Resolve the canonical id before wiring adapter keys, or registry lookups will miss.
notes: Metabolomics portal mixes experimental and theoretical entries; preserve the distinction per record. The data policy states free access but does not itself specify a reuse licence -- do not assign CC0 to this subset.
